public_rationale: The older Reuters Institute study gives the industry-led argument some background support, but it concerns 2018. The post-launch study shows that ChatGPT mentions were far from universal across broad AI coverage. It does not measure OpenAI-only mentions or the generative-AI subset, so it cannot settle the sentence's combined claim. Neither a company-led majority nor the claimed mention rate is established for the relevant population.
limitations: Industry sourcing, industry news pegs, and company control of framing are different measures.
The evidence does not establish the individual reader's news exposure.
The unresolved result holds under both the literal and ordinary readings of 'by default all'.

statement.excerpt: In short, most of the coverage you read on artificial intelligence is led by companies that benefit financially from you thinking artificial intelligence is important and by default all of this coverage mentions OpenAI or ChatGPT.

from_speaker: most of the coverage you read
by default all of this coverage
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns the generative-AI boom since ChatGPT's launch. I use the launch-to-post interval rather than older AI reporting.
'Most' means more than half. 'Led by companies' means companies substantially set the story's agenda or supply its principal framing; merely quoting a company is insufficient.
'By default all' is read as a routine, effectively universal reference to OpenAI or ChatGPT. A literal universal reading is also considered.
The ordinary scope is general news coverage encountered by readers, not only articles selected because they mention ChatGPT.
criteria.support_condition: A representative analysis of the relevant coverage finds a company-led majority and effectively universal mentions of OpenAI or ChatGPT. A literal reading additionally requires no exceptions in the defined population.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A representative analysis finds that company-led coverage is not a majority, or that a substantial share of the relevant coverage mentions neither OpenAI nor ChatGPT. Under the literal reading, a verified in-scope exception defeats the universal component.

evidence.explanation: The study found roughly 60% of news articles pegged to industry in six UK outlets during January–August 2018. This is relevant background, but neither its period nor its broad AI scope matches the claim.

The paper reports ChatGPT mentions in 50–75% of post-launch AI articles at most sampled outlets, with lower shares at three outlets. This cautions against universal wording, but it does not count OpenAI-only mentions or isolate generative-AI coverage.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative pre-post-date corpus coded for company leadership, financial interests, generative-AI scope, and mentions of either OpenAI or ChatGPT.
